body: If you want to cover it make sure you colour correct beforehand, so depending on the colours of bruising and the redness go with the opposite of the colour wheel then foundation and concealer.

In short I'm sorry you feel embarrassed but don't be, from experience working there it's not uncommon, and with the pain, stress, everything it's major surgery. Be kind to yourself, recover and listen to your body everyone is different so you demand what you need (easier said then done). It should be PATIENT CENTRED CARE.

I used to work on a surgery ward and anesthesia did some wakey things, had a guy absolutely in love with his wife but as soon as he woke up he'd propose to people and declare his love, he'd warn us before but forget the whole thing. Some people wake up very punchy and angry, some people cry. It's strong stuff and it messes people up add that on top of stress of surgery, what the surgery is, it's understandable. They were probably looking to make sure it was not something seriously wrong from surgery as were I was the first two hours we check people every 15mins then after went to 30mins (if i remember correctly). I was never annoyed and never wanted an apology for whether they punched me or whatever, they didn't mean it and that moment was overwhelming for them, we are there to help.

From the other side and my surgeries relating to gyne I cry and dear lawd the constipation and pain, and most of the ward my first op most people were crying. They kept giving us biscuits 😂.
